title: Filtered CE pullback construction with concrete resolution abutment
statement: For every scheme $X$ and bounded-below complex $K$ of abelian étale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], choose a termwise hypercohomology presentation $D(X,K)$ [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation]. For every scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$, bounded-below complex $L$ on $Y$ and chain map $v:f^{-1}K\to L$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], there are spectral-sequence maps $M_{f,v}$ [def-sp-spectral-sequence], with $E_1$ map $H^p(v^q)\circ f^*$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. There are simultaneously chosen stabilization bounds $R(X,K,q,n)$ and isomorphisms $e_{X,K,q,n,r}:E_r^{q,n-q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^q H^n(X,K)$ for $r\geq1,R(X,K,q,n)$. For every map $j:f^{-1}\rho_X(K)\to\rho_Y(L)$ of the resolutions in $D$ whose composite with $f^{-1}\rho_X.map$ is homotopic to $v\circ\rho_Y.map$, for every chain map $w:\Gamma(X,\rho_X)\to\Gamma(Y,\rho_Y)$ whose components are the sectionwise inverse-image unit followed by $\Gamma(j)$, there are maps $t_q$ of the finite image-filtration steps commuting with their inclusions and the map $e_{\rho_X}^{-1}H^n(w)e_{\rho_Y}$ on the abutment [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], where $e_\rho$ is the canonical resolution isomorphism of the presentation. For every proof that $t_q$ commutes with successive step inclusions, the stable-page map under $e$ equals the cokernel map induced by $t_{q+1},t_q$. No equality with the derived adjunction unit--Leray composite is asserted.

proof.text: Choose bounded-below Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions and their termwise hypercohomology presentations [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation]. Use canonical signed row identifications and the natural Ext/global-sections comparison, not arbitrary independently chosen row isomorphisms. Shift the bounded-below complex before applying the degree-zero CE existence theorem, then shift the bicomplex back.

Apply exact inverse image and the CE lift to each pair (f,v). Apply the global-sections unit termwise and totalize. This is a filtered chain map for the complex-degree filtration. Apply the canonical filtered spectral-sequence construction, simultaneously for the chosen presentations. Each graded row comparison computes cohomologyMap followed by Sheaf.H.map(v^q); use the same constant-integer/global-section comparison on the rows and resolve the inverse-image row into a target injective resolution. This gives the first-page equation.

For any comparison j between the chosen K-injective resolutions over v up to homotopy, take any supplied chain map w with degreewise components globalSectionsUpperStarMap followed by Γ(j). The parent constructs w and proves its chain-map equation from naturality. The CE total comparison and j represent the same map over the augmentation; bijectivity on homotopy classes into a K-injective target makes them homotopic. Thus the cohomology map of the filtered total is c_X followed by the displayed conjugate of H(w) and c_Y^{-1}. Restrict it to image filtrations and transport along the canonical resolution comparisons to obtain t and ht. No derived unit/Leray comparison is asserted here.

Finite convergence gives stationary cycles and boundaries in each bidegree. Choose presentation-wise stationary bounds R and the canonical quotient-to-image identifications eInf at every later page, using the canonical filtered-complex construction. Its naturality identifies the induced stable-page map with the map on successive quotients of the filtration-step maps. For any proof hc of compatibility, this quotient map is cokernel.map; independence of the proof follows by proof irrelevance. The parent proves hc from ht by cancelling the monic step inclusion.
